page: Vultr vcg-a40-8c-40g-16vram is a Cloud GPU server configured with 8 shared vCPUs based on the Intel x86_64 architecture. The underlying processor features 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz, supported by 16 MB of L3 cache. The system includes 40.0 GB of system memory, providing 5.0 GB per core. For acceleration, it bundles a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU with a 0.3333 allocation and 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is provided by a 740 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results place this server in the top tier for LLM inference tasks using small and medium models. Specifically, prompt processing for a 135M model reaches 9944.32 tokens per second, while text generation achieves 464.42 tokens per second. For a 7B model, prompt processing registers at 3147.67 tokens per second and text generation at 107.73 tokens per second. Standard CPU and memory benchmarks fall within the average range, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 14175.12, a PassMark CPU score of 14090.9, and a Redis SET throughput of 14.91 million operations per second.

The fractional GPU allocation and shared CPU model offer a resource-dense, cost-efficient entry point for workloads requiring GPU acceleration without the expense of a full dedicated GPU. However, the shared CPU allocation and average single-core performance represent a tradeoff for compute-bound tasks. This profile is suited for medium-scale LLM inference, machine learning prototyping, database operations, and applications utilizing GPU-accelerated rendering or data processing.
